Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: REAL production 2D combat projectile and impact sprite atlas, not a mockup. The four creatures in the reference define the approved species materials and soft painterly sprite style. Create a TRANSPARENT landscape 2-column by 4-row atlas of EIGHT isolated small effects, each inside its own equally sized cell, with wide empty transparent gutters and NO characters, no text, no labels, no grid lines, no shadows or glow haze. Rendering must match reference: soft hand-painted dimensional material, thin dark colored contour, upper-left highlights, compact shapes legible when only 10–30 pixels tall. Each sprite must be completely contained in its cell, no cropped trails.
Left column is a RIGHTWARD-moving compact projectile with a short readable material tail; right column is the matching impact burst, slightly wider and low.
Row 1 SPR0UT MATERIAL: translucent honey-gold plant nectar, rounded sticky golden drop with a tiny green plant membrane at its trailing tip. The impact is five glossy golden sap beads with one tiny green fleck, sticky splatter rather than fire or electricity.
Row 2 SPORE MUSHROOM MATERIAL: a compact cluster of tiny violet, cyan, pink, lime and warm yellow spores, visibly powdery fungal seeds mixed with a few translucent round spore vesicles; an airy short trailing plume. Impact is a restrained round fluffy multicolored spore puff with a handful of tiny bead-like spores; not a magic fireball, not rainbow smoke filling the cell.
Row 3 PEBBLE MATERIAL: dense precious warm amber mineral resin, a plump faceted amber resin globule with three tiny trailing amber beads and ochre stone grains. The impact is a small angular glossy amber splash with a few warm ochre grains, not an explosion or metal fragments.
Row 4 SPRING MATERIAL: clear turquoise cyan water, a pointed rightward water globule with two tiny trailing aqua beads, the same watery cyan shading as the water creature. The impact is a shallow outward-spreading aqua water splash with a clear curved rim and four small droplets.
The atlas is meant to be cleanly cropped into these EIGHT game sprites, all with real alpha transparency. Concentrate every effect in the middle 60 percent of its own cell. Keep left-column projectiles consistently oriented with the sharp leading end to the RIGHT and tiny trailing material to the LEFT. Dark empty pixels must be transparent, not a painted dark background. No motion blur that destroys the material.
